# Packets Packet network allows you to send instructions to specific devices remotely. It's a crucial tool in any sort of automation.
## Packet devices Each device that can receive packets requires 2 variables to access them: - Frequency: Represented as a number. Only available to Chief Engineer. Similar devices have the same frequency - Address: Represented as a 4-digit hex code (0x0000) Can be obtained by probing device using packet network configurator. Every address is unique
You can interact with packet devices by using packet network configurator.
Packet network configurator has 2 modes that can be switched on Alt-Z: - Probe: If the correct frequency picked - displays device address and their network. - Save. Saves device in order to create network. Network have their own address.
In order to get frequencies into packet network configurator, you have to either scan CE's frequencies original paper or scan single frequency written on any paper.
# Executor Executor is a complex device that utilizes packets by running code.
Executor uses JavaScript as it's main programming language. It's best if you get familiar with it before working with executor.
Executor has 3 buttons: - KILL: Kills any active processes in the engine. - EXEC: Directly executes the code, has 5-second cooldown. - UPDT: Loads device call definitions into right panel.
## Basic commands
- log(object): Logs the result in code output panel. - frequency(frequency, operation): allows or denies packets from specific frequencies. Operations can be "ALLOW" or "DENY". - send_signal(frequency, address, portName): Sends signal to specified device. - listen(portId, functionName): Assigns port ID (as a number) to existing method. When that port will receive signal - it will execute the method. - get_network(address): Returns network of devices as an address array. Useful for bulk interactions.
## Async
Executor fully supports async execution. In order to use async methods, you must create async function ("async function fn()", as an example).
However, async execution also introduces micro-delay (usually 50ms) to every device call, as opposed to normal execution being instant.
There are few async methods: - sleep(ms): Halts the execution for specific amount of milliseconds. - data_send(frequency, address, object)/receive: Used for exchanging data between executors. Receiving executor halts the execution till he receives the data.
## Device calls In order to interact with the device, you need to create a call object, usually its done like that:
[color=#40C040]"var deviceCall = new LathePrintCall();"[/color]
There are 2 types of device calls: - State: Gets state of the device. Usually you don't parse arguments into it (refer to definitions panel). It is used to get information from the device - Call: Tells the device what to do based on arguments you parse in (refer to definitions panel).
In our case, parsing argument would look like that:
[color=#40C040]"deviceCall.Recipes = {"Igniter"}; deviceCall.Quantity = {1};" (Use square brackets in executor, instead)[/color]
After you finish initializing your call, you have to now call it. In order to do that, you should use "call(frequency, address, deviceCall)" method:
[color=#40C040]"call(frequency, address, deviceCall)";[/color]
If everything is done right, your lathe will successfully print a single igniter!
## Widgets
Have you ever wanted to build your own control panel for all your packet devices? It is possible with widgets.
The main object is Widget that has only ID as its argument in constructor. Widget all stores all widget elements with "Elements" field
[color=#40C040]"var widget = new Widget("EngiControl");"[/color]
[color=#40C040]"widget.Elements = {Element1, Element2};"[/color] Parses the elements into widget.
[color=#40C040]"init_widget(widget);"[/color] Will initialize the widget.
### Widget elements
Every widget element has these properties: - Id: Represented as a string, acts as a unique identifier for each widget element. Do not assign same ID to two widget elements. - Margin: Represented as integer array with 4 arguments ({left, top, right, bottom}). It forms a transparent border on each side to separate itself from other elements. - Size: Represented as integer array with 2 arguments ({X, Y}). Assigns a size to widget element, mostly used for buttons and panels. - HorizontalAligment: Represented as string with specific allowed arguments (Stretch/Left/Center/Right). - VerticalAligment: Represented as string with specific allowed arguments (Strech/Top/Center/Bottom).
Any widget element initializes with ID, just like the Widget.
You can reload widget element by using "update_element(widgetElement)" if you changed it in any way.
### WidgetButton
This widget element is responsible for executing specific method on click. It has following extra arguments: - Text: Represented as a string, assings the text that will be displayed on the button. - MethodName: Represented as a string, name of the method that will be executed upon clicking.
### WidgetContainer
This widget element is capable of storing widget elements inside itself. It has same arguments as Widget itself (Elements as an Array of WidgetElement)
### WidgetLabel
This widget element is responsible for displaying text. It has "Text" as its only argument.
### WidgetTextEdit
This widget element allows you to type in text and then use it in methods. It has "ReadOnly" as its argument, represented as boolean.
When you click on any button, arguments from this widget will be parsed into the executor as "VAR_IdOfWidgetTextEdit", allowing you to use contents of this element.
However, this will work only if button and the text edit are in the same panel.
## Examples:
### Making 30u of bicaridine in chemmaster.
[color=#40C040]var freq = 916;
[color=#40C040]var addr = "0xE63D"
[color=#40C040]var chemCall = new ChemMasterTransferCall();
[color=#40C040]chemCall.Mode = "Transfer";
[color=#40C040]chemCall.FromBuffer = true;
[color=#40C040]chemCall.Reagents = {"Carbon", "Sugar", "Oxygen"};
[color=#40C040]chemCall.Amount = {10, 10, 10};
[color=#40C040]call(freq, addr, chemCall);
